Error.description: 400 invalid request; 401 missing/incorrect configured API key or invalid/expired session; 403 forbidden or unverified LAN identity when no API key is configured; 404 absent resource; 405 unsupported method; 409 CA changed; 413 body over endpoint limit (1 KiB, or 64 KiB for diagnostics); 415 wrong media type; 500 persistence failure; 503 starting/reloading. Route/method errors and missing certificates may be plain text.

NodeHealth.description: Canonical observation state shared by status and selectors. Probe activity and physical dormancy are separate.

mitm_test_generation.description: Current MITM verification generation; present only when interception tests are available. Discard only MITM results when it changes. HTTPS acceptance depends on the CA fingerprint.

mitm_test_origins.description: Exact virtual HTTPS origins allowed for MITM challenges. CA trust is checked independently with a fresh-leaf challenge on the current API socket.

CertificateTest.description: A one-minute CA trust challenge bound to the source IP, router IP and initiating page origin. A POST response is not proof; GET requires a TLS handshake using a leaf issued after challenge creation.

MITMTest.description: A one-minute transparent MITM challenge bound to the verified caller and current interception configuration. At most 8 challenges and observations are retained per verified MAC and 256 globally; excess creation requests return 503. Observations are not a device-wide CA trust verdict; the browser must receive and validate the matching proof over HTTPS with normal certificate verification.

DeviceStatus.description: The requesting device's MAC-attributed upstream paths. IPv4 and IPv6 share the MAC identity. Counters survive reload and reset on daemon restart. Kernel passthrough, local HTTP/DNS responses and daemon-originated work are excluded; splice deltas are included.

states.description: For checked groups, 10 oldest-first buckets spanning the last hour (6 minutes each); the worst state in each bucket. Unchecked groups have no history.

networks.description: Network order: tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6.

selected_node_ids.description: Network order: tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6.

LatencyStats.description: Successful probe durations only. Failures and selection offsets are excluded; average_10 uses the last ten successful samples.

tracking.description: Group-local scheduling role. Standby paths may still be monitored by another group; active operations are reported by recovery.

recovery_elapsed.description: Successfully verified observation time, in nanoseconds.

failure_recovery.description: Required recovery observation duration, in nanoseconds.

score.description: Selection score in nanoseconds; may be negative.

BufferMemoryStatus.description: Process-wide MITM body buffer budget. Byte counters measure reserved buffer storage; denied counts rejected reservations.

limit.description: Configured byte limit. Lowering it does not revoke existing reservations, so used may temporarily exceed limit.

peak.description: Peak reserved bytes over the process lifetime.

denied.description: Rejected reservation count over the process lifetime (unsigned 64-bit integer).

enabled.description: Enabled flag from the accepted configuration. Disabled instances are not instantiated and do not prepare resources.

declared_scopes.description: Number of HTTP scopes declared by the instantiated plugin. Disabled instances do not evaluate Plan and report zero.

http_active.description: Effective scopes can participate in HTTP processing. This does not guarantee that a device is intercepted or that background tasks are healthy.

http_reason.description: Empty when HTTP processing is active; otherwise disabled, no_scopes, mitm_disabled, prepared, draining, or unavailable.

scopes.description: Number of effective HTTP scopes after applying the host-wide HTTP enablement setting.

details.description: Administrator-only plugin-defined JSON report, omitted for user and anonymous LAN access. Its schema belongs to the plugin; reports exclude configuration credentials but can contain private script output.

default.description: Router configuration for this device. It applies when override is null and again after the override is cleared.

abort.description: Abort established connections during reload or suspend; invalid for refresh.

executable_pid.description: Local reload only. Must match the authenticated Unix peer PID. Compare that process's executable contents with the daemon; replace the process if different. Omit for configuration-only reload.

replace.description: Force local process replacement even when the executable matches. Requires executable_pid. Replacement closes old connections before same-PID exec and rebuilds the runtime under blocking guards.

module.description: Required when the script name is not unique within the instance.

mac.description: MITM-enabled target device MAC for a script with LAN isolation enabled. Omission always selects local execution. Scripts with LAN isolation disabled reject MAC selection; omit mac.

from_mac.description: Source device: a nonzero unicast six-byte MAC, distinct from to_mac.

to_mac.description: Destination device: a nonzero unicast six-byte MAC with no existing storage partition.

ScriptTaskStatus.description: One effective execution-scope row for a plugin-managed script definition. Surge always includes a local row and adds device rows only for scripts with LAN isolation enabled; unknown is not an executable target. Times and counters describe this scope's latest scheduled or manual attempt, including execution-slot waits. Only cron has a schedule and timezone; generic is ready when idle and active. Runtime success does not imply application-level success; errors are credential-free categories. Counters and history reset on reload.

scope.description: Effective execution scope, not original request origin. Surge reports local or device explicitly; shared LAN execution is local.

mac.description: Host-confirmed target device MAC; present only when scope is device.

last_error.description: Stable failure or skip category, such as timeout, canceled, error, http_client_unavailable, device_disabled or device_query_failed. No raw script exceptions or response bodies.

skipped.description: Schedule ticks merged during pending discovery or while this task was waiting/running, plus admitted tasks skipped because device eligibility was revoked or device discovery failed.

NodeEgress.description: Local connection to the first proxy, independent of destination network support.

dormant.description: The physical transport has been released and is not being recreated. Omitted when false; independent of group-local selection tracking.

failing.description: Confirmed networks whose latest probe failed; they serve no traffic until a probe succeeds. Capability stays in support. Network order: tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6. Omitted when no network fails.

support.description: Network order: tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6.

download_bytes.description: Unsigned 64-bit count; JavaScript clients must account for integer precision above 2^53-1.

upload_bytes.description: Unsigned 64-bit count; JavaScript clients must account for integer precision above 2^53-1.

checked_at.description: Completion time of the last test; absent before the first completed test. Untracked results are historical.

checking.description: A test is queued/running, or the monitored node awaits its initial check. Untested dormant nodes are not checking.

name.description: Saved logical path name, including its entrance choice.

status.description: Missing or ambiguous preferences remain saved while the startup choice is used temporarily.

track_all.description: Read-only group track_all configuration. False by default: only the selected node is monitored. Configure the file and reload to change it.

default_node_id.description: Present only for an explicitly indexed selector(n). Plain selector has no configured default and cannot be reset.

overridden.description: A saved preference exists, including when it is temporarily missing or ambiguous.

auth_mode.description: User or administrator Bearer credentials, anonymous verified LAN user access, or local Unix administration.

outbound.description: Name of an instantiated, checked outbound. Applies to selector and automatic policies, and checked direct-node targets.

node_id.description: Path ID within that outbound. Empty or omitted probes every path once.

node_ids.description: Accepted targets, including requests coalesced with queued/running checks. Acceptance is not a health result.

compiled_plugins.description: Plugin types registered by the running daemon, sorted by name and independent of instance configuration. Excludes the system MITM diagnostic plugin.

buffer_memory.description: Process-wide body buffer budget, present even when no plugin instances are active.

direct_fallback_connections.description: Process-lifetime count of no-connectivity fallbacks to direct established in userspace; excludes fallback flows forwarded directly by eBPF. Preserved across reloads. Not a per-path or per-node counter.

networks.description: Network order: tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6.

uptime.description: Server-observed elapsed time since started_at in nanoseconds, from the process statistics clock; preserved across reloads.

TableUsage.description: Shared snapshot of kernel tables and userspace resource pools, including the unbounded domain registry. A full evicting table is normal; reject means new entries cannot be admitted.

scope.description: Where the table or resource pool is maintained.

on_full.description: Capacity behavior: evict existing entries (LRU), reject new entries, omit excess kernel projection candidates, or retain without a capacity limit.

error.description: When nonempty, used is unavailable and must not be rendered as zero usage or 0%.

pending.description: Pending kernel projection updates or removals.

candidates.description: IP states with a nonzero domain bitmap before capacity selection. candidates - used is the number excluded by kernel capacity.

limit.description: Maximum entries or resources; zero means no capacity limit.

used.description: Current entries or resources; resident IPs for domain-kernel and retained domain-IP pairs for domain-registry. Unavailable when error is nonempty.

domains.description: Distinct retained domain names, including evidence not projected into the kernel.

ips.description: Distinct retained IPs across all domains; equals ipv4 + ipv6. A shared IP counts once.

ipv4.description: Distinct retained IPv4 addresses, not domain-IP pairs.

ipv6.description: Distinct retained IPv6 addresses, not domain-IP pairs.

gc.description: Pairs removed by time-based GC, cumulative across reload and reset on cold start. Unsigned 64-bit count; JavaScript clients must account for integer precision above 2^53-1.

download_bytes_per_second.description: Oldest first; completed 5-second averages in bytes/second. Both directions have equal length, 0–12 samples.

items.description: Unsigned 64-bit count; JavaScript clients must account for integer precision above 2^53-1.

upload_bytes_per_second.description: Oldest first; completed 5-second averages in bytes/second. Both directions have equal length, 0–12 samples.

items.description: Unsigned 64-bit count; JavaScript clients must account for integer precision above 2^53-1.

ResourceRef.description: Unsigned resource identifiers; generations are comparable only within the same owner and resource.

retry_at.description: Actual timer deadline, present only during backoff. Omitted when no retry timer is owned.

FailureSnapshot.description: Classified failure metadata; message is display text and must not be used as a metric label.

bearerAuth.description: The raw api.user_key or api.admin_key. TCP credentials require HTTPS.

browserSession.name: __Host-dae-session
browserSession.description: Seven-day, host-bound signed session issued only by raw-key login. Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, SameSite=Strict; no Domain. Browser origins must be same-site and approved by web_origins (same-origin by default).

pprofBasic.description: pprof only: username dae and password api.admin_key. Requires HTTPS.

info.description: Status schema 15. Tables report kernel and userspace capacity, full-table behavior and optional usage errors; a full LRU table normally evicts rather than rejecting new entries. Direct fallback connections are a single process-lifetime counter outside path statistics. Node latency includes successful probes only; selection reports degradation and scoring independently. Domain tables report distinct retained domain/IP counts, kernel candidates and time-based GC; limit zero denotes unbounded userspace retention. User and administrator APIs on api.listen, disabled by default. A port binds configured LAN interfaces; an explicit IP:port binds that address. The mode-0600 Unix socket always provides local administration. Administrator credentials include user privileges. Device identity is independent of privileges and requires verified LAN ingress. Mutations require X-Dae-API: 1. JSON APIs reject query parameters. web_origins restricts all browser origins, defaulting to same-origin; cross-site management requests are rejected. Browsers use HttpOnly session cookies, tools use raw keys. Reverse proxies require HTTPS upstream, the literal upstream Host, preserved Origin and X-Dae-Proxy: 1. Forwarding headers only remove LAN/self and browser-trust-proof capabilities; they never grant identity. Plain HTTP is limited to CA bootstrap operations. A challenge proof requires HTTPS. Unix peer credentials authorize local administration independently of TCP security schemes.

post.summary: Trigger an existing cron or generic task
post.description: Requires administration. Returns 202 with an acceptance snapshot, status.scope, device-only status.mac and a per-scope task run number; execution uses daemon routing and continues after the HTTP response. Inspect plugin status for completion. Omitted mac always selects local execution without requiring LAN discovery, MITM or a CA. Explicit mac selects a currently MITM-enabled device only when the script isolates LAN clients; otherwise omit mac. Concurrent triggers for the same waiting/running scope or an explicitly selected disabled device return 409. Does not change its timer schedule. Unknown task/instance: 404; ambiguous name, invalid MAC or MAC selection on a non-isolated script: 400; inactive worker, unavailable device discovery, or canceled/timed-out admission: 503. Admission follows request and worker cancellation and has its own script-timeout budget, separate from accepted execution; discovery does not count as a run. Accepted tasks survive request cancellation. No inline scripts, source URLs, argument overrides or automatic retries.

post.summary: Move one device script storage partition
post.description: Requires administration and a live plugin storage runtime. Synchronously moves all persistentStore keys from one device MAC to another in this instance, preserving keys and values and removing the source partition. No merging or overwriting: even an empty destination partition conflicts. Stop old-MAC traffic and background eligibility first. Device authorization, isolation, local storage, notifications and task counters are unchanged. A later execution for the old MAC can create a new partition. Source and destination need not be online or MITM-enabled. In-memory mode moves only current runtime data. The fixed five-second context bounds cancellable lock waits, not filesystem I/O. Busy protection covers this daemon and overlapping reload generations; stop script writers in other processes sharing the file. No automatic retries: timeout or connection loss does not prove the data was unchanged. A published-but-durability-unconfirmed error means the move already took effect.

200.description: Partition moved; no stored values are returned

400.description: Invalid JSON or MACs, including equal MACs

404.description: Instance or source partition not found

409.description: Destination partition exists or a source/destination script is executing

500.description: Migration failed, or was published but durability is unconfirmed; do not automatically retry

503.description: Storage capability/runtime unavailable, retired instance or canceled/timed-out lock wait

post.description: Requires administration. Uses the outbound's configured DNS probe, existing concurrency bounds and timeouts. No arbitrary URL, network, or timeout overrides are accepted. node_id selects one path; omission or an empty value selects all paths. Returns 202 immediately with accepted IDs; repeated requests for queued/running work coalesce. Selector results are available through GET /api/selectors (checking/tested/checked_at/healthy/latency_ms); other outbounds publish their runtime health and latency through GET /api/status. This is not a persistent probe job and does not change selection or monitoring configuration. Unknown outbound: 404; invalid node/body: 400; unchecked builtin: 409.

get.summary: Read the latest resource refresh and next automatic check
get.description: Requires administration. Reports the latest API or automatic refresh. History is reset on daemon restart. Empty request body.

post.description: Requires administration and an empty request body. Uses the accepted configuration and attempts all downloads regardless of update intervals; does not read configuration edits from disk. Returns 202 immediately; poll GET /api/operations/{id} for this request’s completion. Concurrent queued/running refreshes return 409. Refreshes and reloads publish serially. Invalid candidates leave the current runtime active; available validated snapshots can be used on download failure.

Requires administration. Returns a unique operation ID immediately; poll GET /api/operations/{id} for the result. Reload reads configuration from disk; suspend disables interception; refresh uses the accepted configuration. Operations execute serially. The queue holds at most 16 pending operations; a full queue or a duplicate pending refresh returns 409. Local Unix operation routes remain available throughout plane replacement.

get.description: Requires administration and an empty body. IDs are unique across restarts. The daemon retains the 64 most recently finished operations plus active and queued work; unknown or expired IDs return 404. A client timeout does not cancel accepted work.

put.description: Exchange a raw user or administrator key over HTTPS for a seven-day HttpOnly Cookie session scoped to the API host and role. The response never exposes the credential to JavaScript. Existing sessions, anonymous LAN access and Unix socket identity cannot issue or renew a session. Key rotation invalidates sessions for that role.
